title: Outlook for Mac: Purview DLP wait-on-send support
summary: Hold: the DLP rule command omits the sensitivity-label and recipient conditions Microsoft requires for the documented oversharing dialog. The roadmap details and the distinction between documented Windows controls and unconfirmed Mac settings are supported.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans Purview DLP wait-on-send support for Outlook for Mac.
claims.quote: Outlook for Mac will support Microsoft Purview Data Loss Prevention (DLP) wait-on-send policies.

claims.where: summary; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: The Mac-specific switch and timeout control are not yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Outlook Mac wait on send DLP default licensing price roles DLPWaitOnSendTimeout. Opened Mac policy-tip reference, preferences-outlook and Set-OrganizationConfig; no Mac wait-on-send switch or timeout setting found.

claims.where: controls[0].note; What's changing; Governance controls; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft has not confirmed that the Exchange wait-on-send parameters govern Outlook for Mac.
claims.quote: Searched: Outlook Mac wait on send DLP default licensing price roles DLPWaitOnSendTimeout. Read Set-OrganizationConfig and the Mac and new Windows Outlook policy-tip references; applicability is documented for Windows and web, not Mac.

claims.claim: No documentation ties the classic Outlook registry or Group Policy wait setting to Outlook for Mac.
claims.quote: Searched: Outlook Mac wait on send DLP default licensing price roles DLPWaitOnSendTimeout. Read dlp-osp-get-started, dlp-ol365-win32-policy-tips and preferences-outlook; no Mac applicability for the registry or Group Policy control found.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Open questions
claims.claim: The Mac timeout bypass and Send anyway behaviour are not yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Outlook Mac wait on send DLP default licensing price roles DLPWaitOnSendTimeout. Read Mac, new Windows and classic Outlook policy-tip references and Set-OrganizationConfig; no Mac timeout override behaviour found.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not said whether the documented classic Outlook immediate-send behaviour also describes Mac.
claims.quote: Searched: Outlook Mac wait on send DLP default licensing price roles DLPWaitOnSendTimeout. Read Mac policy-tip reference and oversharing guide; the immediate-send explanation is not attributed to Mac.

claims.claim: Roles for the Mac wait-on-send setting itself are not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Outlook Mac wait on send DLP default licensing price roles DLPWaitOnSendTimeout; "Outlook" "Mac" "wait on send" "roles". Read Mac policy-tip reference, preferences-outlook and Set-OrganizationConfig; no Mac wait-on-send role requirement found.

claims.claim: No admin-centre UI path is documented for the Exchange wait-on-send parameters.
claims.quote: Searched: "DLPWaitOnSendEnabled" "admin center". Read Set-OrganizationConfig and dlp-policy-reference-new-outlook; the latter says the experience is controlled solely through the Exchange parameters and gives no UI path.

claims.claim: Set-OrganizationConfig -DLPWaitOnSendEnabled $true -DLPWaitOnSendTimeout <seconds> configures the documented Exchange organisation control.
claims.quote: $true: Mail sent from Outlook for Windows to Exchange is evaluated by DLP. To set the timeout value, use the DLPWaitOnSendTimeout parameter.

claims.claim: The Mac policy-tip policy is under Microsoft 365 Apps admin center > Customization > Policy Management.
claims.quote: you must enable the policy listed in the following section in the Microsoft 365 Apps Admin Center. ... You can access this policy under Customization and Policy Management.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance controls; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Enable Purview Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policy tips in Outlook governs whether policy tips show in Outlook for Mac.
claims.quote: Enable Purview Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policy tips in Outlook | (default) Disabled policy tips aren't shown Enabled policy tips are shown

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance controls; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: The policy-tip policy can target individuals or groups.
claims.quote: You can target policies to individuals or groups, so you can test and deploy policy tip UI as needed through your organization.

claims.claim: Policy-tip UI is off by default in Outlook for Android, iOS and macOS until the admin policy enables it.
claims.quote: Policy Tip UI is turned off by default in Outlook for Android, iOS, and macOS to allow for administrators to test and perform user training prior to deployment.

claims.claim: No API equivalent is documented for this policy-tip enablement policy.
claims.quote: Searched: "Cloud Policy" "API" "policy" Microsoft 365 Apps PowerShell; "Enable Purview Data Loss Prevention" "Graph" "PowerShell". Read Mac policy-tip reference and overview-cloud-policy; no configuring API or cmdlet found.

claims.claim: Exchange-location DLP policies are managed at Microsoft Purview portal > Data loss prevention > Policies.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Data loss prevention > Policies

claims.claim: The printed New-DlpComplianceRule call is sufficient to create the documented pre-send dialog rule.
claims.quote: To configure oversharing pop-ups with default text, the DLP rule must include these conditions: Content contains > Sensitivity labels > choose your sensitivity label(s) and one or more of the following recipient-based conditions
claims.fix: Replace controls[2].api.call and the rendered command with the full documented warn-rule example: New-DlpComplianceRule -Name <name> -Policy <policy> -NotifyUser Owner -NotifyPolicyTipDisplayOption "Dialog" -ContentContainsSensitiveInformation @(@{operator = "And"; groups = @(@{operator="Or";name="Default";labels=@(@{name=<Label GUID>;type="Sensitivity"})})}) -ExceptIfRecipientDomainIs @("contoso.com","microsoft.com"). The current call omits the required label and recipient configuration; mentioning the omitted parameters in the note does not supply them to the command. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/dlp-osp-get-started.

claims.claim: The cited pre-send dialog documentation does not confirm Mac support.
claims.quote: Searched: Outlook Mac wait on send DLP default licensing price roles DLPWaitOnSendTimeout. Read dlp-osp-get-started and Mac policy-tip reference; the former names Outlook for Microsoft 365, and the latter's oversharing section names Android and iOS, not Mac.

claims.where: Scope; controls[2].note; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: The documented oversharing and wait-on-send setup uses a DLP policy scoped to Exchange.
claims.quote: To enable these pop-ups, first scope your policy to the Exchange location and then select the Show policy tip as a dialog for the user before send option

claims.claim: Learn names the option Show the policy tip as a dialog for the end user before send (available for Exchange workload only).
claims.quote: Select Policy tips > Show the policy tip as a dialog for the end user before send (available for Exchange workload only).

claims.claim: The oversharing guide requires policy creators and deployers to belong to one of the five role groups listed in the briefing.
claims.quote: The account you use to create and deploy policies must be a member of one of the following role groups: Compliance administrator; Compliance data administrator; Information Protection; Information Protection Admin; Security administrator

claims.claim: Outlook for Microsoft 365 wait on send can be enabled using the dlpwaitonsendtimeout registry key.
claims.quote: After you've configured the Oversharing dialog, you can optionally enable the Wait on send dialog feature using the dlpwaitonsendtimeout Registry key (DWORD value).

claims.claim: The corresponding Group Policy setting is Specify wait time to evaluate sensitive content.
claims.quote: You can set this RegKey via group policy, Specify wait time to evaluate sensitive content, script, or other mechanism for configuring registry keys.

claims.claim: New Outlook for Windows wait on send is controlled through DLPWaitOnSendEnabled and DLPWaitOnSendTimeout.
claims.quote: The wait-to-send experience is controlled solely through the following Exchange mailbox parameters: DLPWaitOnSendEnabled ... DLPWaitOnSendTimeout

claims.claim: The mobile and Mac reference's wait-on-send section says Android and iOS do not yet support it, without naming macOS in that statement.
claims.quote: Outlook for Android and iOS doesn't yet support DLP Wait-to-Send

claims.claim: For the documented classic Outlook configuration, a message is sent immediately when wait on send is not configured.
claims.quote: When dlpwaitonsendtimeout isn't configured, the message isn't checked before the user sends it. The email message is sent immediately once Send is clicked.

claims.claim: In that immediate-send case, the DLP service evaluates the message afterwards.
claims.quote: The email message is sent immediately once Send is clicked. The DLP data classification service evaluates the message

claims.claim: The DLP service applies the policy actions in that immediate-send case.
claims.quote: The DLP data classification service evaluates the message and apply the actions defined in the DLP policy.

claims.claim: For Outlook for Microsoft 365, a timeout from 0 to 9999 seconds offers Send anyway if evaluation has not completed in time.
claims.quote: If the policy evaluation doesn't complete in the specified time a Send anyway button appears allowing the user to bypass the presend check. The T value range is 0 to 9999 seconds.

claims.claim: For that registry-based configuration, timeout values above 9999 are replaced with 10000.
claims.quote: If the T value is greater than 9999, it's replaced with 10000

claims.claim: For that above-9999 registry configuration, no Send Anyway override is offered and the message waits until evaluation completes.
claims.quote: the Send Anyway button doesn't appear. This holds the message until the policy evaluation completes and doesn't provide the user with an override option.

claims.claim: For new Outlook for Windows, timeout 0 immediately shows Send Anyway.
claims.quote: When DLPWaitOnSendTimeout = 0, user will immediately see “Send Anyway” in the infobar of mail.

claims.claim: The oversharing guide says matched block rules block the message regardless of the Policy tips configuration.
claims.quote: If the block rules defined in the DLP policy are met, the message will be blocked regardless of how Policy tips is configured.

claims.claim: Classic Outlook evaluation duration can vary with internet speed, content length and the number of policies.
claims.quote: The duration for completing the evaluation can vary depending on factors such as internet speed, content length, and the number of policies defined.

claims.claim: Some users can encounter policy evaluation messages more frequently than others.
claims.quote: Some users may encounter policy evaluation messages more frequently than others, depending on the policies that are deployed on their mailbox.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions
claims.claim: The cited oversharing guide says oversharing pop-ups require a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription.
claims.quote: Oversharing pop-ups require a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription, along with a version of Outlook that supports oversharing pop-ups.

Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/office365/servicedescriptions/microsoft-365-service-descriptions/microsoft-365-tenantlevel-services-licensing-guidance/microsoft-purview-service-description.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The Outlook for Microsoft 365 reference lists wait on send as applying to Online E5 users.
claims.quote: Wait on Send dialog support for Oversharing for Outlook for Microsoft 365 ... Applies to: Online E5 users with connected experience enabled

claims.claim: That Outlook for Microsoft 365 wait-on-send applicability requires connected experience enabled.
claims.quote: Online E5 users with connected experience enabled

claims.claim: Learn's warn-rule example includes ContentContainsSensitiveInformation and ExceptIfRecipientDomainIs in addition to the parameters printed in the briefing.
claims.quote: ContentContainsSensitiveInformation ... At least one label is mandatory. ... ExceptIfRecipientDomainIs ... List of trusted domains.

claims.claim: The described change inserts evaluation into sending a user's message rather than introducing autonomous message creation or sending.
claims.quote: Organizations can require a DLP evaluation before an email is sent and configure how long users must wait for policy evaluation to complete.
